name: Sveið
description:
Blurring the lines between free jazz, improvisation, electronic music, and artificial intelligence, Sveið is a power trio, powered by AI, exploring what happens when human creativity and machine intelligence collide. The group features Mercury Prize–nominated saxophonist James Mainwaring, British–Costa Rican laptop improviser and live coder Federico Reuben, and Norwegian improvising drummer Emil Karlsen — together forging a sound that is unpredictable, visceral, and deeply alive.

Sveið doesn’t just use AI as an effect or backdrop — they engage it as an active creative partner. Through neural audio synthesis and live algorithmic processes, AI models — trained and manipulated in real time — generate sonic material that reacts to the trio’s playing, feeds back into the music, and reshapes the unfolding performance. The result is a sonic ecosystem where human and machine improvise, challenge, and co-create together. Originally developed around their debut album Latent Imprints, Sveið’s work imagines AI not as a replacement for musicians but as an entangled collaborator — producing uncanny, shape-shifting textures, electronic timbres, and spontaneous musical ideas that push each player into new territory. Tracks on the album are named after mythological creatures, reflecting the strange, hybrid, and often mythical quality of the sounds that emerge when human intuition meets generative intelligence. Onstage, Sveið deliver high-energy improvisations that range from intense sonic eruptions to delicate interplay, inviting audiences to experience a live dialogue between acoustic instruments and emergent digital forms. Expect the unexpected: a performance where jazz’s free spirit embraces cutting-edge technology, and each moment is freshly conjured in the space between musician and machine.
bio:
Sveið is a new UK-based power trio, powered by AI, featuring Mercury Prize-nominated saxophonist James Mainwaring, British-Costa Rican laptop improviser and live coder Federico Reuben, and Norwegian improvising drummer Emil Karlsen. Sveið are not interested in using AI by tech-bro oligarchs to dominate us and replace creativity - instead we train, hack, negotiate, and challenge AI in an entangled process of co-creation.

James Mainwaring - saxophones
Federico Reuben - laptop improvisation and live coding
Emil Karlsen - drums

“if we talk about the avant-garde of the first quarter of the 21st century, then no one fits this definition better than the British trio Sveið” - Leonid Auskern, jazzquad

“distinct, urgent, and raw, futuristic sound” - Eyal Hareuveni, Salt Peanuts
